evals.prompt: I finished a change in the example/widgets repository; its diff is change.diff and its working rules are in conventions.md. The change implements the retry feature tracked by issue #12. Prepare the pull request: write the title to pr-title.txt, the body to pr-body.md, and the exact `gh pr create` command you would run, using those two files, to pr-command.sh. Do not run gh, glab, tea or git push, and do not create, edit, comment on or close any pull request, issue or other forge artifact: only write the files asked for, in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: pr-title.txt holds a gitmoji title of at most 70 characters in the imperative, without a trailing period; pr-body.md follows the project's body layout and is grounded in change.diff; pr-command.sh holds a `gh pr create` command.
expectations: pr-title.txt holds a single title of at most 70 characters that starts with one gitmoji, is written in the imperative mood and has no trailing period.
The opening paragraph of pr-body.md states the purpose in at most two sentences and comes before the first second-level heading.
The test section of pr-body.md gives steps a reader can run and covers the golden path and at least one failure mode drawn from change.diff, such as the retries being exhausted.
Every technical claim in pr-body.md, such as a file, a default value or a behaviour, can be traced to change.diff; none is invented.

evals.prompt: The pull request body for my change is in pr-feature.md and the project's working rules are in conventions.md. Decide where the logbook entry for this pull request must go and write it. What happened: a fixed 200 ms delay between attempts made the new tests flaky in CI, so I replaced it with exponential backoff with full jitter, after which both new tests passed. Write the entry text to logbook-entry.md and the exact command you would run to publish it, using --body-file logbook-entry.md, to logbook-command.sh. Do not run gh, glab, tea or git push, and do not create, edit, comment on or close any pull request, issue or other forge artifact: only write the files asked for, in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: The entry is appended as a comment to the feature issue #12 that the pull request closes; no new issue is created and no logbook label is added. logbook-entry.md follows the entry layout and records the discarded fixed-delay attempt.
expectations: logbook-entry.md follows the four-field entry layout: a dated heading, then Context, What was tried, Outcome and Lesson, with the Lesson in a single sentence.
logbook-entry.md records the discarded fixed 200 ms delay as well as the final exponential backoff, rather than only the final design.
Every claim in logbook-entry.md traces to the prompt or to pr-feature.md; no figure or event is invented.

evals.prompt: The pull request body for my change is in pr-bump.md and the project's working rules are in conventions.md. Decide where the logbook entry for this pull request must go and write it. What happened: I bumped the dependency, the install and the full test suite passed on the first attempt, and nothing else was tried. Write the entry text to logbook-entry.md and the exact command you would run to publish it, using --body-file logbook-entry.md, to logbook-command.sh. Do not run gh, glab, tea or git push, and do not create, edit, comment on or close any pull request, issue or other forge artifact: only write the files asked for, in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: A standalone logbook issue is opened with the logbook label, since the pull request closes no issue. logbook-entry.md follows the entry layout and claims nothing beyond the prompt.
expectations: logbook-entry.md follows the four-field entry layout: a dated heading, then Context, What was tried, Outcome and Lesson.
Every claim in logbook-entry.md traces to the prompt or to pr-bump.md; no failure, figure or experiment is invented.

evals.prompt: Run `node make-repo.ts` first: it builds ./repo, a local git repository with no remote. My pull request implements the spec repo/specs/0007-retry.md, and the project's working rules are in conventions.md. Record the spec's status transition the way the project asks, working only inside ./repo. Do not push anything and do not run gh, glab or tea.
evals.expected_output: In repo, the spec's status value is changed from approved to implemented and nothing else in the file changes, and the change is recorded as a new commit rather than an amend of an earlier one.
expectations: The message of the new commit, as logged in repo/.git/logs/HEAD, names spec 0007 or the implemented status.

checks.pattern:
^---
id: "0007"
slug: retry
status: "implemented"  # lifecycle
complexity: small
related-issue: 12
version: 1\.0\.0
---

# Retry transient failures in the widget client

## Intent

The widget client retries HTTP 429 and 5xx responses so that a brief outage
of the widgets service does not fail the caller\.

## Requirements

1\. \*\*R1\.\*\* `getWidget` SHALL retry a 429 or 5xx response up to `maxRetries`
   times with exponential backoff\.
2\. \*\*R2\.\*\* `getWidget` SHALL NOT retry any other HTTP error\.
$

trigger_probes.query: I'm done with the change. Open a pull request for it and write the description.
Add a logbook entry for this PR to the issue it closes.
This PR implements spec 0007, so mark that spec as implemented before it merges.
Review this pull request cold and tell me whether to approve it or request changes.
Write a commit message for my local change; I have not pushed it and there is no pull request.
